newsitem.title: ITALY: FORECAST - Italy money mkt rate cut hopes evaporate.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Italy money mkt rate cut hopes evaporate.

text.p: Italy's money market sees no sign of an official interest rate cut in the near term and appears to be taking no medium term position, according to a weekly study of implicit rates carried out for Reuters by the Bocconi University's research arm, Igier.
The study showed the market sees the overnight rate in one month's time and on a three-month horizon slightly higher than it did one week ago but the variation was too small to signal a new trend.
The market saw o/n at 7.07 percent in one month's time, against 6.97 percent forecast last week. On Tuesday, the day Igier based its study, o/n stood at 7.17 percent.
On a three-month timeframe, the implicit o/n rate was seen at 6.92 percent, slightly up from 6.79 percent seen a week ago. A month ago it was seen at 7.21 percent.
On a one-year horizon, the implicit o/n rate was seen rising to 6.73 percent compared with 6.67 percent seen last week. A month ago it was seen at 7.12 percent.
But on a two-year view, the implicit o/n rate was seen falling slightly to 7.06 percent from 7.17 percent seen last week. A month ago it was seen at 7.47 percent.

The spread between Italian and German implicit o/n rates on a two-year timeframe, considered a good indicator of market confidence in Italy's entry into the European economic and monetary union (EMU), was in at 237 basis points from 245 bps a week ago and from 263 bps a month ago.
